$comment: Drives two scripts. bootstrap.sh writes AWS SSO profiles into ~/.aws/config; tunnel.sh opens the SSM tunnels. Environments reference profiles BY NAME, so tunnel.sh never needs account/role details directly. Replace every placeholder (myorg, myproject, account IDs, sso_start_url) with your own.

defaults.$comment_sso: Details for the [sso-session <name>] block bootstrap.sh writes. Skip bootstrap entirely if you use plain IAM profiles — just make sure each env's profile below already exists in ~/.aws/config.
defaults.$comment_bastion: How tunnel.sh finds the jump host: it looks up a running EC2 instance whose Name tag equals this template with {env} substituted. Must match the module's `name` output.

$comment_profiles: bootstrap.sh creates one profile per (account, role) pair. Name = profile_name_template with {account} (key from accounts) and {role_short} (from roles[]). Defaults below produce e.g. myorg-dev-admin, myorg-prod-admin.
$comment_environments: tunnel.sh reads this. Each env references a profile BY NAME (must exist in ~/.aws/config). Every resource is opt-in via enabled. Discovery is name/tag based — the first matching resource whose identifier contains the env name wins.
$comment_ports: Local ports auto-allocate from base_port. Resources on 443 and 5432 route through HAProxy by SNI so the real hostname resolves locally and certificate validation still passes. Everything else is a direct local-port tunnel.

eks.$comment: Discovered via aws eks list-clusters; first cluster whose name contains the env name wins. Writes a kubeconfig context at ~/.kube/config-tunnel.

internal_alb.$comment_tags: Tag-based discovery. {env} is substituted. Any one tag set matching wins.
internal_alb.$comment_sni: If sni_hosts is empty, tunnel.sh reads the ALB listener host-header rules and routes each via HAProxy SNI.

aurora.$comment: Aurora cluster endpoint via describe-db-clusters; first cluster whose ID contains env name wins. Routed through the 5432 SNI frontend.

rds_proxy.$comment: RDS Proxy via describe-db-proxies; first proxy whose name contains env name wins. Routed through the 5432 SNI frontend.

postgres.$comment: Standalone RDS PostgreSQL instance, as opposed to an Aurora cluster. Routed through the 5432 SNI frontend, so sslmode=verify-full still works.

mysql.$comment: Standalone RDS instance. Set engine to mysql or mariadb. Direct local port, so connect to 127.0.0.1 rather than the RDS hostname.

redis.$comment: ElastiCache Serverless (Redis/Valkey) via describe-serverless-caches. Direct local port.

redis_cluster.$comment: Classic (non-serverless) ElastiCache replication group. Uses the configuration endpoint when cluster mode is enabled, the primary endpoint otherwise.

memcached.$comment: ElastiCache memcached cluster, via its configuration endpoint.

documentdb.$comment: DocumentDB cluster endpoint. Connect with directConnection=true, since replica set discovery would hand back in-VPC hostnames.

opensearch.$comment: OpenSearch domain with a VPC endpoint. Routed through the 443 SNI frontend.
opensearch.$comment_dashboards: This also covers OpenSearch Dashboards, the Kibana-style UI. A VPC domain serves it from the same endpoint on the same port, at https://<domain-endpoint>/_dashboards, so the one tunnel gives you both the REST API and the browser UI. No separate entry needed.

msk.$comment: MSK, first TLS bootstrap broker only. Enough to bootstrap a client; a producer that follows metadata to the other brokers needs each of them forwarded too.

resources.$comment_custom: Anything else reachable from the bastion: a self-managed database on EC2, a peered partner endpoint, an internal service by IP. host and port are required. Set sni_443 true to route it through the HAProxy 443 frontend instead of a direct port.
